title: HTML Resume Generator

Format distinct dynamic output lines for the scan initiation time, the target ip address, the resolved hostname, the specific open port information, the filtered port information, the total closed port count, the operating system signature guess, and the physical hardware address.

title: Curl Command Script Generator
spec: Write a function `curl(endpoints)` that generates a shell script of network requests. Accept a list of endpoints where each is a tuple of a request method, a destination url, a bearer token, a content type, a data payload, a user agent string, an output destination, and a timeout value. Return a list of formatted string lines representing the commands. Format distinct dynamic output lines for the method flag, the destination url string, the authorization bearer token header, the content type header, the data payload flag, the user agent string flag, the output destination flag, and the maximum timeout seconds flag.

title: Flight Itinerary Ticket Formatter
spec: Write a function `ticket(flights)` that produces a plain text boarding pass. Accept a list of flights where each is a tuple of a passenger name, a record locator, a flight number, an origin airport, a destination airport, a departure time, an arrival time, and a seat assignment. Return a list of formatted string lines for the printed document. Format distinct dynamic output lines for the full passenger name, the alphanumeric record locator, the specific flight number, the route combining origin and destination, the scheduled departure time, the scheduled arrival time, the assigned seat, and the boarding group identifier.

title: BBCode Forum Post Builder
spec: Write a function `bbcode(posts)` that outputs a formatted message board string. Accept a list of posts where each is a tuple of a topic title, an author name, a main text body, an image link, a quote source, a code language identifier, a font size modifier, and a text color hex. Return a list of formatted string lines representing the markup. Format distinct dynamic output lines for the bolded topic title, the italicized author name, the main text body, the bracketed image link, the quote block attributing the source, the code block specifying the language, the font size wrapper, and the text color wrapper.

title: Regex Pattern Compiler Text
spec: Write a function `regex(patterns)` that constructs a verbose regular expression document. Accept a list of patterns where each is a tuple of a group name, a literal prefix, a character class, a minimum repetition count, a maximum repetition count, a literal suffix, an optional character, and a description comment. Return a list of formatted string lines representing the verbose expression. Format distinct dynamic output lines for the named capture group definition, the literal prefix match, the character class boundary, the repetition range combining minimum and maximum, the literal suffix match, the optional character notation, a word boundary assertion, and the description comment.

title: Github Actions YAML Text Builder
spec: Write a function `workflow(jobs)` that creates a continuous integration script. Accept a list of jobs where each is a tuple of a workflow name, a branch trigger, a job identifier, a runner operating system, a python version, a script execution step, an artifact name, and a cron schedule string. Return a list of formatted string lines representing the automation file. Format distinct dynamic output lines for the workflow name declaration, the branch push trigger, the job identifier block, the runner operating system assignment, the python version setup, the script execution command, the artifact upload name, and the cron schedule expression.

title: Man Page Document Formatter
spec: Write a function `manpage(commands)` that writes a traditional manual text file. Accept a list of commands where each is a tuple of a tool name, a version number, a short description, a syntax usage string, a long description, a primary flag detail, an author name, and a related tool reference. Return a list of formatted string lines for the manual. Format distinct dynamic output lines for the header combining tool name and version, the short description section, the syntax usage section, the long description text, the primary flag explanation, the author attribution, the related tool reference, and a copyright footer.

title: ASCII Art Histogram Chart
spec: Write a function `histogram(data)` that builds a text based statistical chart. Accept a list of data points where each is a tuple of a chart title, a vertical label, a horizontal label, a category name, a bar representation string, a numeric value, a total sum, and a percentage calculation. Return a list of formatted string lines representing the visualization. Format distinct dynamic output lines for the centered chart title, the vertical axis label, the horizontal axis label, the left aligned category name, the graphical bar representation, the right aligned numeric value, the total sum footer, and the percentage of total annotation.

title: OpenVPN Client Profile Builder
spec: Write a function `openvpn(clients)` that generates a secure tunnel configuration. Accept a list of clients where each is a tuple of a profile name, an interface type, a network protocol, a server address, a server port, a certificate file path, a key file path, and a cipher algorithm. Return a list of formatted string lines representing the profile. Format distinct dynamic output lines for a comment containing the profile name, the interface device type, the chosen network protocol, the remote endpoint combining address and port, the certificate file path directive, the private key file path directive, the data cipher algorithm, and the authentication digest algorithm.

title: Wireguard Interface Text Builder
spec: Write a function `wireguard(peers)` that builds a peer to peer network configuration file. Accept a list of peers where each is a tuple of an interface address, a listen port, a private key, a peer public key, an allowed network range, an endpoint address, an endpoint port, and a keepalive interval. Return a list of formatted string lines for the settings text. Format distinct dynamic output lines for the interface address assignment, the local listen port, the interface private key, the peer public key declaration, the allowed network ip range, the remote endpoint combining address and port, the persistent keepalive interval, and a routing table index comment.

title: Robot Framework Script Builder
spec: Write a function `robot(tests)` that generates an automation suite file. Accept a list of tests where each is a tuple of a suite name, a library import, a variable name, a variable value, a test case identifier, an action step, a verification step, and a documentation string. Return a list of formatted string lines representing the test script. Format distinct dynamic output lines for the suite name header, the external library import statement, the variable definition combining name and value, the test case identifier block, the keyword action step, the result verification step, the specific documentation string, and a test timeout value line.

title: Kubernetes Deployment YAML Builder
spec: Write `build(deployment)` that takes a dictionary of deployment parameters. Extract the string application name, integer replica count, string container image, integer port number, string namespace, string pull policy, and string service account. Return a single text string containing a valid YAML deployment manifest. The text must include an api version of apps slash v1, a kind of Deployment, metadata containing the application name and namespace, and a spec defining the replica count. The template section must specify the container name, image, pull policy, service account, and container port. Also include a labels section matching the application name for both the metadata and selector match labels.

title: Radius Client Configuration Builder
spec: Implement `generate(clients)` taking a list of network client configuration dictionaries. Each object contains a string client identifier, a string ip address, a string shared secret network password, a string short name, a string client type, an integer connection limit, an integer idle timeout, and a string virtual server name. Return a single multiline string formatted for a radius server setup. For each client, generate a configuration block starting with the word client and the identifier enclosed in braces. Inside the block, assign the ip address, secret, short name, type, limit, timeout, and virtual server to their standard configuration keys, using an equals sign and ensuring each key and value pair occupies its own indented line.

title: SSH Client Configuration Generator
spec: Create `generate(hosts)` which receives a list of host definition dictionaries. Each definition has a string alias, a string hostname or ip address, a string username, an integer port, a string identity file path, an integer timeout, an integer keep alive interval, and a string forward agent flag. Produce a single text string suitable for a standard secure shell client configuration file. For each host, start with the word Host and the alias, followed by indented lines for HostName, User, Port, IdentityFile, ConnectTimeout, ServerAliveInterval, and ForwardAgent using the provided values. Separate each host block with a blank line.

title: GraphQL Mutation String Builder
spec: Write `construct(mutation)` to generate a textual query payload. The input is an object containing a string operation name, a string target entity, a list of string input fields, a list of string return fields, an integer user id, a string client id, a string request identifier, and a string timestamp. Construct a valid query string that declares a mutation operation named after the operation name. Inside, call the target entity passing the user id, client id, request identifier, and timestamp as literal arguments. Pass the input fields formatted as a nested input object where each field is set to a placeholder string variable. Finally, list all the return fields inside curly braces to specify the requested response payload. Return the final multiline string.

title: Windows Batch File Script Builder
spec: Create `script(tasks)` that takes a list of task instruction dictionaries, along with a string script author, a string creation date, and a string environment variable path. Each dictionary contains a string task name, a string executable path, a string working directory, a string log file path, a string priority level, a string error output path, and a string user context. Return a single string representing a complete windows command prompt script. Begin the script with echo off, followed by remark lines stating the script author and creation date. Add a set command appending the environment variable path to the system path. For each task, append an echo command announcing the task name, a title command setting the window title, a change directory command, a run as command specifying the user context, and a start command using the executable path with log and error redirections.

title: OpenSSL Certificate Request Config Generator
spec: Implement `configure(details)` that accepts a dictionary of certificate request parameters. The parameters include an integer key size, a string country code, a string state, a string locality, a string organization name, a string organizational unit, a string common name, a string email address, and a string challenge password. Return a multiline string matching the required initialization format for generating a certificate signing request. The text must include a request block setting default bits to the key size, prompt to no, and distinguished name to a custom block name. Then include the distinguished name block that maps the standard two letter country, state, locality, organization, organizational unit, common name acronyms, and email address to their corresponding input values.

title: CMake Project File Generator
spec: Write `generate(project)` accepting a dictionary describing a native software project. It contains a string project name, a string version number, a string c plus plus standard, a string minimum cmake version, a string executable name, a string source directory path, a string include directory path, and a list of string library dependencies. Return a single multiline string containing the project configuration. The statement must include the cmake minimum required command, the project command using the name and version, and set the standard using the specified c plus plus version. Include directives to add the executable from the source directory, target include directories using the include path, and target link libraries listing all the dependencies.

title: HAProxy Load Balancer Config Builder
spec: Create `build(proxy)` that takes a dictionary containing proxy settings. It includes a string frontend name, a string bind address, an integer bind port, a string default backend name, a string load balancing algorithm, a string health check url, an integer timeout client, an integer timeout server, and a list of backend server tuples containing a string server name, a string server address, and an integer server port. Return a multiline configuration string. Create a frontend section using the frontend name, adding a bind directive with the address and port, a timeout client directive, and a default backend directive. Create a backend section using the backend name, specifying the balance algorithm, the timeout server, an http check request for the health check url, and listing each server with its name, address, port, and the word check.

title: Slurm Cluster Batch Script Generator
spec: Implement `create(job)` receiving a dictionary of computing cluster job requirements. Inputs include a string job name, an integer node count, an integer task count, a string time limit, a string partition name, a string email address, a string standard output file, a string standard error file, and a string command to execute. Output a multiline string representing the batch script. Begin with a standard shell shebang. Add directives starting with the standard cluster hash keyword followed by flags for job name, nodes, tasks, time, partition, output file, error file, and mail user using the provided values. Add another directive to send mail on job end. Conclude the script with a command runner prefix followed by the specified command.

title: Mail Transfer Agent Config Builder
spec: Write `configure(settings)` that accepts a dictionary of mail server settings. It provides a string hostname, a string domain, a list of string network interfaces, a list of string destination domains, a string trusted network subnet, an integer message size limit, a string mailbox transport protocol, a string smtpd banner, and a string relay host. Return a single multiline string representing the configuration file. Set myhostname to the hostname, mydomain to the domain, and myorigin to use the domain variable. Join the network interfaces and destination domains with commas and assign them to their respective configuration keys. Assign the subnet to the networks key, the message size limit to its key, the mailbox transport protocol, the smtpd banner, and the relay host.

title: Terminal Multiplexer Session Script Builder
spec: Create `script(session)` taking a dictionary defining a terminal workspace. It contains a string session name, a string starting directory, a string custom prefix key, a string layout style, an integer default pane count, and a list of window tuples each holding a string window name and a string startup command. Return a bash script as a single string. First, add a command to start a new detached session with the specified session name and starting directory. Next, add a command to set the prefix key. For each window, add a command to create a new window in the session with its name, apply the layout style, and split it into the default pane count. Add commands to send the startup command followed by a carriage return to the respective window target. Add a final command to attach to the session.

title: Firewall Ruleset Script Generator
spec: Implement `generate(firewall)` that takes a dictionary containing a string primary network interface, a string management ip address, an integer management port, a string logging prefix, and a list of rule dictionaries. Each rule has a string chain name, a string protocol, a string source address, a string destination address, an integer destination port, a string jump target, and a string text comment. Return a multiline shell script string. Start with commands to set the default interface variable, flush all existing rules, allow incoming connections from the management ip on the management port, and add a logging rule using the logging prefix. For each rule in the list, construct an append command specifying the chain, protocol, source address, destination address, destination port, jump target, and the text comment enclosed in quotes.

title: Serialization Protocol Array Builder
spec: Write `serialize(command)` that accepts a list of string arguments representing a command for an in memory data store, plus a string transaction id, a string database index, a string client name, an integer execution timeout, a string consistency level, and an integer replica count. Return a single string formatted according to the standard serialization protocol for arrays. Start the output with a series of comment lines, outputting one line for each of the transaction id, database index, client name, execution timeout, consistency level, and replica count using a hash symbol prefix. Then append an asterisk followed by the total number of arguments and a carriage return line feed sequence. For each argument, append a dollar sign, the length of the string argument, and a carriage return line feed sequence, immediately followed by the string argument itself and another carriage return line feed sequence.

title: Media Transcoder Command Builder
spec: Create `build(transcode)` which receives a dictionary of media conversion settings. It includes a string input path, a string output path, a string video codec, a string audio codec, an integer video bitrate in kilobits, an integer audio bitrate in kilobits, an integer frame rate, a string resolution, a string encoding preset, and an integer constant rate factor. Return a single string containing the full command line execution string. Start with the tool name and specify the input file. Add the video codec flag, the video bitrate flag formatted with a trailing k, the frame rate flag, the video size flag, the encoding preset flag, and the constant rate factor flag. Add the audio codec flag and the audio bitrate flag formatted with a trailing k. End the string with the output path.

title: Metrics Agent Plugin Config Generator
spec: Implement `generate(plugins)` accepting a list of input plugin configuration dictionaries. Each dictionary contains a string plugin name, an integer collection interval in seconds, an integer timeout in seconds, a string data format, a string user agent, a list of string target urls, and a string authorization token. Return a single multiline string in standard minimal configuration language format. For each plugin, create a double bracketed section header using the plugin name. Beneath it, set the interval appending a lowercase s for seconds, set the timeout appending an s, specify the data format, set the user agent, and list the urls formatted as an array of double quoted strings. Add an HTTP headers section defining the authorization header with the provided token.

title: Log Processing Pipeline Config Builder
spec: Write `configure(pipeline)` that takes a dictionary containing a string input port, a string input type, a string match field, a string match pattern, a string target index, a string elasticsearch template name, an integer pipeline worker count, and a list of string elasticsearch hosts. Return a multiline configuration string. Create a global settings block defining the pipeline worker count. Create an input block containing a beats listener set to the input port and type. Create a filter block containing a grok processor that matches the specified match field against the match pattern. Create an output block containing an elasticsearch destination that sets the hosts array using the provided hosts, sets the index name using the target index, and assigns the template name.

title: Domain Name System Zone File Generator
spec: Create `build(zone)` that receives a dictionary of domain records. It includes a string domain name, a string admin email replacing the at symbol with a dot, an integer serial number, an integer refresh rate, an integer retry rate, an integer expiry time, an integer minimum time to live, a string primary name server, and a list of address records containing a string subdomain and a string ip address. Return a single multiline string representing a complete zone file. Include the time to live directive at the top. Generate the start of authority record using the domain name, primary name server, admin email, and all the timing integers properly enclosed in parentheses. Add a name server record and an internet address record for each item in the address list.

title: Network Share Configuration Builder
spec: Implement `generate(shares)` which takes a list of network share configuration dictionaries. Each has a string share name, a string directory path, a string comment, a string valid users list, a string invalid users list, an integer maximum connections limit, a boolean read only flag, and a boolean guest ok flag. Return a single multiline configuration string. The output must start with a global section setting the workgroup to workgroup and security to user. For each share, create a section header enclosed in square brackets using the share name. Below it, set the path, add the comment, set the valid users and invalid users, define the maximum connections, and output yes or no for the read only and guest ok settings based on their boolean values.

title: Code Documentation Block Generator
spec: Write `document(function)` that accepts a dictionary detailing a software function. It includes a string function name, a string brief description, a list of tuples containing a string parameter name and string parameter description, a string return description, a string author name, a string date, a string version number, and a string deprecation warning. Return a multiline string representing a complete block comment. Start the block with a double asterisk comment opener. Add a brief directive followed by the brief description. For each parameter in the list, add a param directive followed by the parameter name and its description. Add return, author, date, version, and deprecated directives using their respective values. Close the block with an asterisk slash.

title: Monitoring Agent Command Config Builder
spec: Create `configure(checks)` receiving a list of monitoring check dictionaries. Each contains a string command name, a string plugin executable name, an integer warning threshold, an integer critical threshold, a string execution user, an integer timeout in seconds, an integer maximum retries count, and a string additional arguments payload. Return a multiline configuration string. For each check, output a line starting with command enclosed in square brackets containing the command name, followed by an equals sign. On the same line, append the standard absolute path to the plugins directory, a slash, the plugin executable name, a warning flag with its threshold, a critical flag with its threshold, the timeout flag, the retries flag, the user flag, and finally the additional arguments payload.

title: Package Build Script Generator
spec: Implement `generate(package)` that accepts a dictionary of software package metadata. It contains a string package name, a string version, an integer release number, a string description, a string architecture, a string source url, a string software license, a string maintainer name, a list of string dependencies, and a string build command. Return a single multiline string defining the package build variables. Set the standard name, version, and release variables. Enclose the description in double quotes. Enclose the architecture in single quotes inside parentheses. Enclose the source url in double quotes inside parentheses. Set the license and maintainer variables. Format the dependencies as a space separated list of single quoted strings inside parentheses. Create a build function block containing the build command.

title: Web Server Virtual Host Builder
spec: Write `build(host)` taking a dictionary of web server settings. It provides a string ip address, an integer port, a string server name, a string server alias, a string document root path, a string error log path, a string custom log path, a string admin email address, and a string directory index file. Return a single multiline string. Open a virtual host tag using the ip address and port. Inside the block, specify the server name, server alias, and server admin email directives. Specify the document root directive enclosed in double quotes. Add the directory index directive using the provided file name. Specify the error log and custom log directives enclosed in double quotes, ensuring the custom log ends with the standard combined format label. Close the virtual host tag.

title: File System Snapshot Replication Script
spec: Create `script(replication)` which receives a dictionary of backup instructions. It includes a string source pool, a string source file system, a string snapshot name, a string remote user, a string remote host, a string destination pool, a string destination file system, a string ssh private key path, and an integer bandwidth limit in megabytes. Return a multiline bash script string. Start with a command to create a recursive snapshot on the source pool and file system using the snapshot name prefixed with an at symbol. Follow with a command that sends the newly created snapshot, pipes it into a secure shell connection using the remote user, remote host, and private key path, and receives it forcefully into the destination pool and file system, limiting the stream bandwidth using the provided integer. Finally, add a command to log the snapshot name and current date.

title: System Monitor Config Generator
spec: Implement `generate(monitor)` taking a dictionary of desktop monitor settings. Inputs include a string alignment position, a string background color, an integer update interval, a string font name, an integer font size, an integer window border width, a string window transparency level, and a list of hardware sensor tuples containing a string label and a string hardware variable. Return a multiline string in the required script format. Create a configuration table assigning the alignment, background color, update interval, border width, transparency level, and font formatted with its name and size. Create a text block enclosed in double square brackets. Inside the text block, iterate over the hardware sensors to output a formatted string for each, combining the display label with the corresponding hardware variable enclosed in dollar sign and curly braces.

title: Traffic Grapher Router Config Builder
spec: Write `build(router)` that accepts a dictionary of network traffic monitoring parameters. It contains a string router name, a string ip address, a string snmp community, a string contact email, a string physical location, a string working directory, a string log format, an integer refresh interval, and a list of integer interface ids. Return a single multiline string. Output global configuration directives for the working directory, the log format, and the refresh interval. For each interface id, output a target directive setting the object identifier for incoming and outgoing traffic separated by an ampersand, followed by a colon, the community string, an at symbol, and the ip address. Output a max bytes directive using an arbitrary bandwidth limit. Output a title directive combining the router name and interface id. Output directives for the contact email and physical location. Finally, output a page top directive generating standard HTML header tags that display the router name and interface id.

title: Asterisk Dialplan Builder
spec:
Write `dialplan(contexts)`. The input is a list of tuples representing context configurations. Each tuple contains a context name string, a caller identifier string, an integer for timeout seconds, a mailbox string, an included context string, and a boolean for call recording. The function must return a list of formatted configuration lines. For each tuple, generate a bracketed context header, a comment stating the context name, a caller identifier setting line, a timeout line using the integer, a voicemail setup line for the mailbox, an include line for the context, and a mix monitor recording line if the boolean is true. Finally, add a standard hangup line.
Example input: [("sales", "8005551234", 30, "100@default", "internal", True)]
Example output: ["[sales]", "; Context: sales", "exten => s,1,Set(CALLERID(num)=8005551234)", "exten => s,2,Set(TIMEOUT(absolute)=30)", "exten => s,3,VoiceMail(100@default,u)", "include => internal", "exten => s,4,MixMonitor(sales.wav)", "exten => s,5,Hangup()"]

title: Logrotate Configuration Builder
spec:
Write `logrotate(services)`. The input is a list of tuples where each contains a log file path string, a frequency string, an integer for the number of copies to keep, an integer for the size limit in megabytes, an owner user string, an owner group string, an email address string, and a boolean indicating if missing files are okay. Return a list of configuration text lines. For each service, create a global comment mentioning the log file path, a block header with the path and an opening brace, a line for the frequency, a rotate count line using the copies integer, a size limit line appending an M to the integer, a create permissions line with the user and group, a mail destination line, a missing ok directive if the boolean is true (otherwise no missing ok), and a closing brace line.
Example input: [("/var/log/app.log", "daily", 7, 50, "root", "adm", "admin@domain.com", True)]
Example output: ["# Log configuration for /var/log/app.log", "/var/log/app.log {", "    daily", "    rotate 7", "    size 50M", "    create root adm", "    mail admin@domain.com", "    missingok", "}"]

title: Neo4j Cypher Query Builder
spec:
Write `cypher(operations)`. The input is a list of tuples containing an operation type string, a node label string, an integer node identifier, a string property name, a text value, an integer target node identifier, a target label string, and a relationship type string. Return a list of query string lines. If the operation is a match, output a match node line using the label and identifier, and a return line for the property. If it is a create, output a create node line using the label, property name, and text value, and an index line for the label. If it is a relate, output a match line for the source identifier, a match line for the target identifier and label, and a create relationship line using the relationship type.
Example input: [("create", "Person", 1, "name", "Alice", 2, "Department", "WORKS_IN")]
Example output: ["CREATE (n:Person {name: 'Alice'});", "CREATE INDEX ON :Person(name);"]

title: YARA Malware Ruleset Builder
spec:
Write `yara(rules)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a rule name string, an author string, a date string, an integer threat level, a hex pattern string, a text pattern string, an integer file size limit, and a boolean for global scope. Return a list of rule lines. For each rule, generate a rule header optionally prefixed with global if the boolean is true, a meta section header, an author line, a date line, a threat level line using the integer, a strings section header, a hex pattern line with a specific variable identifier, a text pattern line with its identifier, a condition section header, a file size condition line using the integer limit, and a condition matching both string identifiers.
Example input: [("Backdoor", "Alice", "2023-10-01", 5, "4D 5A", "cmd.exe", 1024, True)]
Example output: ["global rule Backdoor {", "meta:", "    author = \"Alice\"", "    date = \"2023-10-01\"", "    threat_level = 5", "strings:", "    $hex_pattern = { 4D 5A }", "    $text_pattern = \"cmd.exe\"", "condition:", "    filesize < 1024KB and $hex_pattern and $text_pattern", "}"]

title: AppArmor Profile Builder
spec:
Write `apparmor(profiles)`. The input is a list of tuples containing an application path string, an attachment profile string, an integer capability number, a read path string, a write path string, an execute path string, a network protocol string, and a boolean for audit mode. Return a list of text lines. For each profile, output an include tunables line, a profile header combining the path and attachment string, a capability line using the integer that prefixes audit if the boolean is true, a read permission line for the read path, a write permission line for the write path, an execute permission line for the execute path, a network access line using the protocol, a deny access line for a temporary folder specific to the application path, and a closing brace.
Example input: [("/usr/bin/app", "app_profile", 2, "/etc/app.conf", "/var/log/app.log", "/usr/lib/app/bin", "tcp", True)]
Example output: ["#include <tunables/global>", "profile /usr/bin/app app_profile {", "    audit capability 2,", "    /etc/app.conf r,", "    /var/log/app.log w,", "    /usr/lib/app/bin ix,", "    network tcp,", "    deny /tmp/app_tmp/** rw,", "}"]

title: Snort Intrusion Detection Rules
spec:
Write `snort(rules)`. The input is a list of tuples containing an action string, a protocol string, a source network string, an integer source port, a destination network string, an integer destination port, a message text, an integer rule identifier, an integer revision number, and a classification string. Return a list of rule text lines. For each tuple, generate a comment line combining the rule identifier and action, the main rule header combining the action, protocol, source network, source port, destination network, and destination port, an opening parenthesis for options, a message line, a signature identifier line using the rule integer, a revision line using the revision integer, a classification line, a content match line using the protocol, a metadata line referencing the rule identifier, and a closing parenthesis.
Example input: [("alert", "tcp", "any", 80, "192.168.1.0/24", 8080, "Suspicious web traffic", 10001, 1, "web-attack")]
Example output: ["# Rule 10001: alert", "alert tcp any 80 -> 192.168.1.0/24 8080", "(", "    msg:\"Suspicious web traffic\";", "    sid:10001;", "    rev:1;", "    classtype:web-attack;", "    content:\"tcp\";", "    metadata:rule 10001;", ")"]

title: Vagrantfile Configuration Builder
spec:
Write `vagrant(machines)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a machine name string, a box name string, an integer for memory allocation, an integer for cpu count, an ip address string, a host folder string, a guest folder string, and an integer for forwarded port. Return a list of configuration lines. For each machine, generate a machine definition block header using the name, a box assignment line, a private network line using the ip address, a synced folder line combining host and guest folders, a forwarded port line using the port integer, a provider block header, a memory assignment line using the memory integer, a cpu assignment line using the cpu integer, a virtualbox name assignment line using the machine name, and two end statements to close the blocks.
Example input: [("webserver", "ubuntu/focal64", 1024, 2, "192.168.33.10", "./src", "/var/www", 8080)]
Example output: ["config.vm.define \"webserver\" do |webserver|", "  webserver.vm.box = \"ubuntu/focal64\"", "  webserver.vm.network \"private_network\", ip: \"192.168.33.10\"", "  webserver.vm.synced_folder \"./src\", \"/var/www\"", "  webserver.vm.network \"forwarded_port\", guest: 80, host: 8080", "  webserver.vm.provider \"virtualbox\" do |vb|", "    vb.memory = \"1024\"", "    vb.cpus = 2", "    vb.name = \"webserver\"", "  end", "end"]

title: DHCPd Configuration Builder
spec:
Write `dhcp(subnets)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a subnet string, a netmask string, a router ip string, a dns ip string, a domain name string, an integer for minimum lease time, an integer for maximum lease time, a start ip string, and an end ip string. Return a list of text lines. For each subnet, output a subnet declaration header using the subnet and netmask, an option routers line using the router ip, an option domain name servers line using the dns ip, an option domain name line using the domain name string, a default lease time line using the minimum lease integer, a maximum lease time line using the maximum lease integer, a range line combining start and end ips, a host declaration line for a gateway using the router ip, a log statement echoing the subnet string, and a closing brace.
Example input: [("10.0.0.0", "255.255.255.0", "10.0.0.1", "8.8.8.8", "local.lan", 600, 7200, "10.0.0.10", "10.0.0.50")]
Example output: ["subnet 10.0.0.0 netmask 255.255.255.0 {", "  option routers 10.0.0.1;", "  option domain-name-servers 8.8.8.8;", "  option domain-name \"local.lan\";", "  default-lease-time 600;", "  max-lease-time 7200;", "  range 10.0.0.10 10.0.0.50;", "  host gateway { fixed-address 10.0.0.1; }", "  log(info, \"Configured 10.0.0.0\");", "}"]

title: Git Config File Builder
spec:
Write `gitconfig(profiles)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a profile name string, a full name string, an email address string, an editor command string, a signing key string, an integer for cache timeout, a proxy url string, and a boolean for fast forward pulls. Return a list of configuration lines. For each profile, generate a comment line stating the profile name, a user section header, a name assignment line, an email assignment line, a signing key assignment line, a core section header, an editor assignment line, a credential cache timeout line using the integer, a proxy line using the proxy url, and a pull fast forward line set to true or false based on the boolean.
Example input: [("Work", "John Doe", "john@work.com", "vim", "ABC12345", 3600, "http://proxy:8080", True)]
Example output: ["# Profile: Work", "[user]", "\tname = John Doe", "\temail = john@work.com", "\tsigningkey = ABC12345", "[core]", "\teditor = vim", "[credential]", "\thelper = cache --timeout=3600", "[http]", "\tproxy = http://proxy:8080", "[pull]", "\tff = true"]

title: Maven POM XML Generator
spec:
Write `pom(projects)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a group identifier string, an artifact identifier string, a version string, an integer for java compiler version, a main class string, a dependency group string, a dependency artifact string, and a dependency version string. Return a list of xml tags. For each project, generate a project opening tag, a group identifier tag, an artifact identifier tag, a version tag, a properties section containing compiler source and target tags using the compiler integer, a build section block specifying a main class tag using the main class string, a dependencies section opening tag, a dependency block combining the dependency group, artifact, and version strings into their respective tags, and closing tags for the dependencies, build, and project elements.
Example input: [("com.example", "app", "1.0.0", 17, "com.example.Main", "org.slf4j", "slf4j-api", "1.7.32")]
Example output: ["<project>", "<groupId>com.example</groupId>", "<artifactId>app</artifactId>", "<version>1.0.0</version>", "<properties>", "<maven.compiler.source>17</maven.compiler.source>", "<maven.compiler.target>17</maven.compiler.target>", "</properties>", "<build><mainClass>com.example.Main</mainClass></build>", "<dependencies>", "<dependency>", "<groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>", "<artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>", "<version>1.7.32</version>", "</dependency>", "</dependencies>", "</project>"]

title: Xorg Server Config Builder
spec:
Write `xorg(monitors)`. The input is a list of tuples containing an identifier string, a driver string, an integer for refresh rate, an integer for screen width, an integer for screen height, an integer for color depth, an option string, and a bus identifier string. Return a list of configuration lines. For each monitor, generate a monitor section header, an identifier line, a refresh rate line using the integer, a device section header, a device identifier line by appending the word device to the identifier string, a driver line using the driver string, a bus identifier line using the bus string, a screen section header, a default depth line using the color depth integer, a display modes line combining the width and height integers, and an option line using the option string.
Example input: [("Monitor0", "nvidia", 60, 1920, 1080, 24, "DPMS", "PCI:1:0:0")]
Example output: ["Section \"Monitor\"", "    Identifier \"Monitor0\"", "    Option \"TargetRefresh\" \"60\"", "EndSection", "Section \"Device\"", "    Identifier \"Monitor0-device\"", "    Driver \"nvidia\"", "    BusID \"PCI:1:0:0\"", "EndSection", "Section \"Screen\"", "    DefaultDepth 24", "    SubSection \"Display\"", "        Modes \"1920x1080\"", "        Option \"DPMS\"", "    EndSubSection", "EndSection"]

title: Squid Proxy ACL Configurator
spec:
Write `squid(policies)`. The input is a list of tuples containing an access control name string, an ip network string, a domain name string, an integer for a port, an integer for maximum connections, a days of week string, a time range string, and a boolean for granting access. Return a list of configuration lines. For each policy, output an access control line for the ip network using the name string, a line for the domain name using the name string, a port line using the integer port, a maximum connections line using the integer, a time range line combining the days of week and time range strings, an http access line that allows or denies based on the boolean applying to the name string, a cache allow line using the name string, a log format string referencing the name string, and an access log line applying the name string.
Example input: [("office", "10.0.0.0/8", ".example.com", 8080, 100, "MTWHF", "09:00-17:00", True)]
Example output: ["acl office src 10.0.0.0/8", "acl office dstdomain .example.com", "acl office port 8080", "acl office maxconn 100", "acl office time MTWHF 09:00-17:00", "http_access allow office", "cache allow office", "logformat office_fmt %ts.%03tu %6tr %>a %Ss/%03>Hs %<st %rm %ru %[un %Sh/%<a %mt", "access_log daemon:/var/log/squid/office.log office_fmt office"]

title: Apache Tomcat server.xml Builder
spec:
Write `tomcat(connectors)`. The input is a list of tuples containing an integer for a port, a protocol string, an integer for a redirect port, an integer for maximum threads, an integer for connection timeout, a certificate file path string, a secure protocol string, and a boolean for enabling compression. Return a list of xml tags. For each connector, output a connector opening tag, a port attribute line using the port integer, a protocol attribute line using the protocol string, a redirect port attribute line using the redirect port integer, a maximum threads attribute line using the integer, a connection timeout attribute line using the integer, a compression attribute line toggled on or off based on the boolean, a certificate keystore attribute line using the certificate path string, a secure protocol attribute line using the secure protocol string, and a closing tag.
Example input: [(8443, "HTTP/1.1", 443, 200, 20000, "conf/cert.jks", "TLSv1.2", True)]
Example output: ["<Connector", "  port=\"8443\"", "  protocol=\"HTTP/1.1\"", "  redirectPort=\"443\"", "  maxThreads=\"200\"", "  connectionTimeout=\"20000\"", "  compression=\"on\"", "  keystoreFile=\"conf/cert.jks\"", "  sslProtocol=\"TLSv1.2\"", "/>"]

title: Pip Requirements Text Builder
spec:
Write `requirements(packages)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a package name string, a version string, an integer for python major version, an integer for python minor version, an extra feature string, a cryptographic hash string, a custom index url string, and a boolean for editable installation mode. Return a list of configuration text lines. For each package, generate an index url line using the custom index url string, a package installation line that prepends an editable flag to the package name if the boolean is true, an extra features line enclosing the extra feature string in brackets, a python version marker line combining the major and minor version integers, a hash checking line using the cryptographic hash string, a trailing comment line indicating the python requirement, and a separate echo log line stating the package name and version string.
Example input: [("requests", "2.26.0", 3, 8, "security", "sha256:abcdef", "https://pypi.org/simple", False)]
Example output: ["--index-url https://pypi.org/simple", "requests==2.26.0", "[security]", "; python_version >= '3.8'", "--hash=sha256:abcdef", "# Requires Python 3.8", "echo \"Installing requests 2.26.0\""]

title: Gemfile Dependencies Builder
spec:
Write `gemfile(gems)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a library name string, a version string, an environment group string, an integer for ruby major version, an integer for ruby minor version, a repository url string, a branch name string, and a boolean for lazy loading. Return a list of ruby configuration lines. For each library, output a ruby version declaration line combining the major and minor version integers, a group block header using the environment group string, a library inclusion line combining the library name and version string, a git repository parameter line using the repository url string, a branch parameter line using the branch name string, a require false parameter line if the lazy loading boolean is true, an end block line, and a post install configuration line using the library name.
Example input: [("nokogiri", "1.12.5", "development", 2, 7, "git://github.com/sparklemotion/nokogiri.git", "main", True)]
Example output: ["ruby '2.7.0'", "group :development do", "  gem 'nokogiri', '1.12.5'", "  git: 'git://github.com/sparklemotion/nokogiri.git'", "  branch: 'main'", "  require: false", "end", "Bundle.ui.info 'nokogiri installed'"]

title: Sed Substitution Script Builder
spec:
Write `sedscript(replacements)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a search pattern string, a replacement text string, an integer for a specific line number, an integer for a repeat count, a backup file extension string, a flag string, an error log path string, and a boolean for case insensitive matching. Return a list of command text lines. For each replacement, generate a comment line stating the search pattern, a sed invocation line using the backup extension string, an address range prefix line using the integer line number, a substitution command line combining the search pattern and replacement text, a flag line using the flag string that appends an ignore case flag if the boolean is true, a loop label line using the integer repeat count, a branch command line for the loop, an error writing command line using the error log path, and a print command line showing the replacement text.
Example input: [("foo", "bar", 10, 5, ".bak", "g", "/var/log/sed.err", True)]
Example output: ["# Replace foo", "sed -i.bak", "10", "s/foo/bar/", "gi", ":loop_5", "b loop_5", "w /var/log/sed.err", "p bar"]

title: XHTML Form Document Builder
spec:
Write `xhtmlform(fields)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a field identifier string, a label text string, an input type string, a default value string, an integer for maximum length, an integer for tab index, a placeholder text string, and a boolean for a disabled state. Return a list of xml tags. For each field, generate a form opening tag, a wrapper division tag using the field identifier, a label tag using the label text and field identifier, an input tag specifying the input type and field identifier, a value attribute line using the default value string, a maximum length attribute line using the integer, a tab index attribute line using the integer, a placeholder attribute line using the placeholder string, a disabled attribute line if the boolean is true, and a closing division tag. Example input: [("user", "Username:", "text", "admin", 20, 1, "Enter username", False)] Example output: ["
", "
", "", "", "
", "
"]

title: JSON Schema Validator Text Builder
spec:
Write `jsonschema(properties)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a property key name string, a data type string, a format category string, a description text string, an integer for minimum length, an integer for maximum length, a default value text string, and a boolean indicating if the field is nullable. Return a list of configuration text lines. For each property, generate a quoted string line for the property key name, a type attribute line combining the data type string and the nullable boolean, a format attribute line using the format category string, a description attribute line using the description text string, a minimum length attribute line using the integer, a maximum length attribute line using the integer, a default value attribute line using the default text string, a custom error message attribute line referencing the property key name, and a comment log line using the property key name.
Example input: [("email", "string", "email", "User email address", 5, 100, "none@example.com", True)]
Example output: ["\"email\": {", "  \"type\": [\"string\", \"null\"],", "  \"format\": \"email\",", "  \"description\": \"User email address\",", "  \"minLength\": 5,", "  \"maxLength\": 100,", "  \"default\": \"none@example.com\",", "  \"errorMessage\": \"Invalid email\"", "}", "// Processed email"]

title: XML RPC Request Builder
spec:
Write `xmlrpc(calls)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a method name string, an integer call identifier, a string parameter, an integer parameter, a double parameter string, a boolean flag, an authentication token string, and a timestamp string. Return a list of xml tags. For each call, generate an xml declaration line, a method call opening tag, a method name tag containing the method name string, a custom header tag containing the integer call identifier, a custom authentication tag containing the token string, a custom timestamp tag containing the timestamp string, a parameter tag wrapping the string parameter, a parameter tag wrapping the integer parameter, a parameter tag wrapping the double parameter string, a parameter tag wrapping the boolean flag, and a closing method call tag.
Example input: [("getUser", 101, "admin", 5, "3.14", True, "TOKEN123", "2023-01-01")]
Example output: ["<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>", "<methodCall>", "<methodName>getUser</methodName>", "<header id=\"101\"/>", "<auth token=\"TOKEN123\"/>", "<timestamp time=\"2023-01-01\"/>", "<param><value><string>admin</string></value></param>", "<param><value><int>5</int></value></param>", "<param><value><double>3.14</double></value></param>", "<param><value><boolean>1</boolean></value></param>", "</methodCall>"]

title: SOAP Envelope XML Generator
spec:
Write `soap(requests)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a namespace url string, an action name string, an integer for a transaction identifier, a username string, a password string, a payload data string, a routing url string, and a boolean for the must understand flag. Return a list of xml tags. For each request, generate a soap envelope opening tag specifying the namespace url string, a soap header opening tag, a security token tag containing the username string, a security token tag containing the password string, a routing tag using the routing url string and appending a must understand attribute if the boolean is true, a transaction tag containing the integer transaction identifier, a soap body opening tag, an action tag combining the action name string and namespace url string, a payload tag containing the payload data string, and a closing envelope tag.
Example input: [("http://example.com/ns", "GetBalance", 999, "alice", "secret", "<accountId>123</accountId>", "http://router.local", True)]
Example output: ["<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap=\"http://example.com/ns\">", "<soap:Header>", "<wsse:Username>alice</wsse:Username>", "<wsse:Password>secret</wsse:Password>", "<wsa:To mustUnderstand=\"1\">http://router.local</wsa:To>", "<tx:Id>999</tx:Id>", "</soap:Header>", "<soap:Body>", "<ns:GetBalance xmlns:ns=\"http://example.com/ns\">", "<payload><accountId>123</accountId></payload>", "</ns:GetBalance>", "</soap:Body>", "</soap:Envelope>"]

title: Rsyslog Conf Builder
spec:
Write `rsyslog(rules)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a logging facility string, a severity level string, a destination file path, an integer for a user identifier, an integer for a group identifier, a directory mask string, a file mask string, and a boolean for synchronous writing. Return a list of configuration text lines. For each rule, generate a comment line describing the facility and severity strings, a file owner directive line using the integer user identifier, a file group directive line using the integer group identifier, a directory creation mode line using the directory mask string, a file creation mode line using the file mask string, an action line combining the facility string, severity level string, and destination file path, a synchronization disable line that appends a minus sign to the destination path based on the boolean, a template binding line using the destination file path, and an error handling block referencing the facility string.
Example input: [("mail", "info", "/var/log/mail.log", 100, 100, "0755", "0640", False)]
Example output: ["# Rule for mail info", "$FileOwner 100", "$FileGroup 100", "$DirCreateMode 0755", "$FileCreateMode 0640", "mail.info /var/log/mail.log", "mail.info -/var/log/mail.log", "mail.info;RSYSLOG_TraditionalFileFormat /var/log/mail.log", "if $syslogfacility-text == 'mail' then /var/log/mail.err"]

title: Subversion Authz File Generator
spec:
Write `svnauthz(repositories)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a repository name string, a user group name string, a comma separated user list string, a repository folder path, a permissions string, an integer for a revision limit, an ip address string, and a boolean for read only anonymous access. Return a list of configuration lines. For each repository, generate a comment line stating the repository name, a groups section definition header, a group assignment line combining the user group name and user list string, a repository path header enclosed in brackets using the repository name and folder path, an anonymous access assignment line setting read or none based on the boolean, a group permissions line combining the user group name and permissions string, a revision limit line using the integer, an ip network restriction line using the ip address string, and an alias definition line referencing the repository name.
Example input: [("project_x", "devs", "alice,bob", "/trunk", "rw", 1000, "192.168.1.0/24", True)]
Example output: ["# Access for project_x", "[groups]", "devs = alice,bob", "[project_x:/trunk]", "* = r", "@devs = rw", "revision-limit = 1000", "network = 192.168.1.0/24", "[aliases]", "px = project_x"]

title: Fail2ban Jail Config Builder
spec:
Write `fail2ban(jails)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a jail name string, a service name string, a log file path string, an integer for maximum retries, an integer for find time window, an integer for ban duration, an email address string, and a boolean for ignoring local loopback traffic. Return a list of configuration lines. For each jail, generate a jail header block enclosed in brackets using the jail name, an enabled setting line set to true, a filter setting line using the service name string, a log path setting line using the log file path string, a maximum retries line using the retries integer, a find time line using the find time integer, a ban duration line using the ban integer, an ignore ip line for the local loopback address if the boolean is true, an action line sending notifications to the email address string, and a comment summary line referencing the jail name.
Example input: [("ssh-jail", "sshd", "/var/log/auth.log", 3, 600, 3600, "admin@local", True)]
Example output: ["[ssh-jail]", "enabled = true", "filter = sshd", "logpath = /var/log/auth.log", "maxretry = 3", "findtime = 600", "bantime = 3600", "ignoreip = 127.0.0.1/8", "action = %(action_mwl)s[dest=\"admin@local\"]", "# Configured ssh-jail"]

title: Grub Bootloader Config Generator
spec:
Write `grub(kernels)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a menu title string, a partition identifier string, a kernel image path, an initialization ramdisk path, a root device uuid string, a video mode string, an integer for boot timeout, and a boolean for displaying a splash screen. Return a list of configuration lines. For each kernel, generate a menu entry opening line using the menu title string, a timeout variable setting line using the integer, a search root command line using the partition identifier string, a linux kernel load line combining the kernel image path and root device uuid string, a video payload line using the video mode string, a splash screen argument line based on the boolean, an initialization ramdisk load line using the ramdisk path, a closing brace for the menu entry block, and a custom echo log line displaying the menu title string.
Example input: [("Ubuntu", "hd0,msdos1", "/boot/vmlinuz", "/boot/initrd.img", "1234-5678", "keep", 5, True)]
Example output: ["menuentry 'Ubuntu' {", "  set timeout=5", "  search --no-floppy --fs-uuid --set=root hd0,msdos1", "  linux /boot/vmlinuz root=UUID=1234-5678 quiet splash", "  set gfxpayload=keep", "  splashimage=(hd0,msdos1)/boot/splash.xpm.gz", "  initrd /boot/initrd.img", "}", "echo 'Loaded Ubuntu'"]

title: Samba smb.conf Generator
spec:
Write `smbconf(shares)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a share name string, a description text string, a folder path string, a valid users comma separated string, an integer for file creation mask, an integer for directory creation mask, an integer for maximum connections, and a boolean for public access. Return a list of configuration lines. For each share, generate a share header block enclosed in brackets using the share name string, a comment setting line using the description text string, a path setting line using the folder path string, a valid users setting line using the valid users string, a file creation mask line using the integer, a directory creation mask line using the integer, a maximum connections line using the integer, a guest access line set to yes or no based on the boolean, a printable setting line set to no, and an echo test line referencing the share name.
Example input: [("public", "Public Share", "/srv/samba/public", "@users", 644, 755, 50, True)]
Example output: ["[public]", "comment = Public Share", "path = /srv/samba/public", "valid users = @users", "create mask = 644", "directory mask = 755", "max connections = 50", "guest ok = yes", "printable = no", "# Loaded public"]

title: Medical Laboratory Report Builder
spec: Write a program to generate a plain text medical laboratory report. The entry function is `build(patient, tests, doctor)`. The patient information includes the full name, birth date, and medical record number. The tests are provided as a list where each entry has a test name, a measured value, a unit of measurement, and a reference range. The doctor information includes a name and a license number. The output should be a single text document that begins with a clinic header, followed by a formatted section for patient details. Next, generate a table of results where each test is displayed on its own line showing the name, the value with its unit, and the reference range in parentheses. If the value is outside the reference range, append a high or low warning flag to that line. Conclude the report with a summary section indicating the total number of tests performed and a signature block containing the doctor's name and license number. For example, given patient "Alice", doctor "Dr. Smith", and tests `[("Hemoglobin", 14.2, "g/dL", "13.8-17.2")]`, the output should include lines like "Patient: Alice" and "Hemoglobin: 14.2 g/dL (13.8-17.2)".

title: University Transcript Formatter
spec: Create a text generator for an academic transcript. The entry function is `format(student, semesters, degree)`. The student details include the full name, student identification number, and major. The semesters are a list of terms, where each term contains the term name, year, and a list of courses. Each course includes a subject code, course number, course title, credits, and a letter grade. The degree information provides the graduation date and honors if applicable. The generated transcript must start with a university header, followed by the student information block. For each semester, output a term heading, then list each course on a separate line formatting the subject, course number, title, credits, and grade. After listing the courses for a term, display a line showing the total credits earned in that term. Finally, append a summary section showing the overall total credits and a degree award line with the graduation date and honors status. For example, given student "Bob", and a course `("CS", 101, "Intro", 3, "A")`, the output should include lines like "Student: Bob" and "CS 101 Intro - 3 credits (Grade: A)".

title: Redis Configuration Generator
spec: Develop a tool to generate a configuration file for a memory database server. The entry function is `generate(settings)`. The settings provide the bind address, port number, maximum memory limit, maximum memory policy, append only file toggle, password, log file path, and database directory. The output should be a plain text configuration document. Create lines for binding the address and setting the listening port. Add a line configuring the maximum memory limit, and another line for the eviction policy. If the append only setting is true, generate a line enabling it; otherwise generate a line disabling it. If a password is provided, output a line to require the password for clients. Include lines specifying the path to the log file and the working directory. Also generate a comment block at the top indicating the server port and memory limit for quick reference. For example, given settings with port `6379`, memory `"2gb"`, and password `"secret"`, the output should include lines like "port 6379", "maxmemory 2gb", and "requirepass secret".

title: ARFF Dataset Exporter
spec: Write a utility to export tabular data into the attribute relation file format used by machine learning tools. The entry function is `export(relation, attributes, rows)`. The relation is a text string naming the dataset. The attributes are provided as a list containing the attribute name and its data type, such as numeric, string, or a list of nominal categories. The rows represent the actual data entries, where each row is a list of values corresponding to the attributes. The output must begin with a line declaring the relation name. Next, iterate through the attributes and generate an attribute declaration line for each one, formatting it with the attribute name and its type. If the type is a list of nominal values, format them correctly as a comma separated list enclosed in braces. After the attributes, output a line declaring the data section. Finally, iterate through the rows and generate a single line for each row, with all values formatted as comma separated strings. For example, given relation `"iris"`, an attribute `("sepallength", "numeric")`, and a row `[5.1, 3.5]`, the output should include "@relation iris", "@attribute sepallength numeric", and "5.1,3.5".

title: Minecraft Server Properties Builder
spec: Create a configuration file builder for a multiplayer block game server. The entry function is `configure(properties)`. The properties contain the server message of the day, network port, maximum allowed players, game mode, difficulty level, level name, player versus player toggle, and spawn protection radius. Generate a plain text document starting with a comment line indicating it is a generated server properties file. Following this, generate individual lines for each setting. Format the message of the day line, the server port line, and the maximum players line. Output the game mode and difficulty settings on their respective lines. Add a line specifying the level name to load. For the boolean player versus player setting, generate a line setting it to true or false. Finally, generate a line defining the spawn protection radius. Each setting must be formatted as a key and value pair separated by an equals sign, with no extra spaces around the equals sign. For example, given properties with port `25565`, players `20`, and pvp `True`, the output should include lines like "server-port=25565", "max-players=20", and "pvp=true".

title: Vowpal Wabbit Data Formatter
spec: Implement a function to format machine learning training data into a specific text format. The entry function is `format(label, importance, tag, namespaces)`. The label is a numeric class or regression target, the importance is a numeric weight, and the tag is a text identifier for the example. The namespaces contain feature groups, where each group has a name and a list of features. Each feature has a name and a numeric value. The output must be a single text line representing one training example. Start the line by formatting the label, followed by the importance weight and the tag, separated by spaces. Then, for each namespace, append a pipe character followed by the namespace name. For every feature within that namespace, append the feature name, a colon, and the feature value. All these elements must be concatenated into one continuous string per example. For example, given label `1`, importance `1.0`, tag `"ex1"`, and namespaces `[("m", [("h", 1.5)])]`, the output should be "1 1.0 ex1 |m h:1.5".

title: KML Placemark Generator
spec: Write a program to generate geographic markup text for mapping applications. The entry function is `generate(placemarks, document)`. The document provides a title and an overall description. The placemarks are a list where each entry contains a name, a text description, a latitude, a longitude, an altitude, and an icon web address. The output must be a well formed text string starting with the standard markup header and a document opening tag containing the document title and description formatted into appropriate tags. For each placemark, generate a block of text that includes a placemark opening tag, tags for the name and description, and a style tag containing the icon address. Additionally, generate a point tag block that contains a coordinates tag formatting the longitude, latitude, and altitude separated by commas. Close each placemark block, and finally close the document block. For example, given a document title `"My Map"` and a placemark `("Home", "My house", 40.0, -73.0, 10.0, "icon.png")`, the output should include "<name>My Map</name>" and "<coordinates>-73.0,40.0,10.0</coordinates>".

title: FIX Protocol Message Builder
spec: Create a generator for financial information exchange protocol messages. The entry function is `build(sender, target, sequence, message, fields)`. The sender and target are text identifiers, the sequence is an integer, the message is a text code indicating the message type, and the fields are a list containing numeric tag identifiers and their corresponding values. The output must be a single continuous string. Begin by formatting a standard header containing the protocol version tag, the message type tag, the sender tag, the target tag, and the sequence number tag. Each tag and value pair must be joined by an equals sign and separated by the standard protocol delimiter character. Next, format each tag and value pair from the fields list and append them to the string. Finally, compute a checksum of the entire string so far, and append the checksum tag and value at the end. For example, given sender `"CLIENT"`, target `"BROKER"`, sequence `1`, message `"D"`, and fields `[(11, "ORDER1")]`, the output should include "8=FIX.4.2|9=...|35=D|49=CLIENT|56=BROKER|34=1|11=ORDER1|10=...".

title: Borg Backup Script Generator
spec: Develop a tool to generate a shell script for automated system backups. The entry function is `generate(repository, archive, paths, passphrase)`. The repository is a directory or network path, the archive is a text name for the specific backup, the paths are a list of directories to back up, and the passphrase is a security key. The output must be a multiline text script. Start with a standard shell shebang line. Generate a line that exports the passphrase as an environment variable. Next, output a line exporting the repository path as an environment variable. Generate the main backup command line invoking the backup tool with the archive name and formatting all provided paths as arguments. Follow this with a line invoking the prune command to keep only a specific number of recent daily and weekly backups. Generate a line to run the compact command, and finally output an echo command that announces completion of the archive name. For example, given repository `"/backup"`, archive `"daily"`, paths `["/home"]`, and passphrase `"secret"`, the output should include "export BORG_PASSPHRASE=secret" and "borg create /backup::daily /home".

title: Syslog Configuration Builder
spec: Write a program to generate a logging daemon configuration file. The entry function is `build(sources, filters, destinations)`. The sources define origin names and network ports. The filters define filter names, facility names, and priority levels. The destinations define destination names and file paths. The output must be a multiline text document. For each source, generate a block of text defining a network input with its name and port number. For each filter, generate a block defining a facility filter using the filter name, the facility, and the priority level. For each destination, generate a block specifying a file output using the destination name and the file path. Finally, generate log path statements that tie them together: format a line for each combination of source, filter, and destination to route the traffic correctly. For example, given a source `("net", 514)`, a filter `("f1", "auth", "info")`, and a destination `("d1", "/var/log/auth.log")`, the output should include "source net { tcp(port(514)); };" and "log { source(net); filter(f1); destination(d1); };".

title: OpenLDAP Record Exporter
spec: Create a utility to export user information into directory interchange format text. The entry function is `export(users, domain)`. The domain is a base domain string, and the users are a list where each entry contains a username, first name, last name, email address, user identifier number, group identifier number, and login shell. The output must be a continuous multiline text document containing records separated by blank lines. For each user, generate a distinguished name line combining their username with the base domain. Generate lines for the required object classes. Output the common name line by combining the first and last name, and generate the surname line. Generate the user identifier line, the group identifier line, and the email address line. Include lines specifying the home directory path derived from the username, and the login shell path. For example, given domain `"dc=com"`, and a user `("jsmith", "John", "Smith", "j@dc.com", 1000, 100, "/bin/bash")`, the output should include "dn: uid=jsmith,dc=com", "cn: John Smith", and "uidNumber: 1000".

title: NMEA GPS Sentence Generator
spec: Implement a function to generate marine electronics standard text sentences from location data. The entry function is `generate(time, latitude, longitude, satellites, altitude)`. The time is a text string of hours, minutes, and seconds. The latitude and longitude are provided as decimal values, and must be formatted into degrees, minutes, and a cardinal direction letter. The satellites is an integer count, and altitude is a decimal in meters. Generate a standard fix data sentence starting with a specific header, followed by the time, the formatted latitude and its direction, the formatted longitude and its direction, a fix quality indicator, the satellite count, and the altitude with its unit. Calculate the checksum of the sentence content and append it at the end formatted as hexadecimal. Next, generate a recommended minimum specific sentence containing the time, an active status character, the formatted coordinates, a speed of zero, a course of zero, and a date string. Calculate and append the checksum for this second sentence. For example, given time `"123519"`, latitude `48.07038`, longitude `11.31000`, satellites `8`, and altitude `545.4`, the output should include "$GPGGA,123519,4804.2228,N,01118.6000,E,1,08,0.9,545.4,M,46.9,M,,*47".

title: PostScript Vector Graphic Builder
spec: Write a program to generate a page description language file for printing vector graphics. The entry function is `build(title, lines, circles, texts)`. The title is a text string. The lines contain start and end coordinates with line widths. The circles contain center coordinates, a radius, and red, green, and blue color values. The texts contain coordinates, a text string, and a font size. Start the output with a standard header comment, a title comment formatting the provided title, and a bounding box comment. For each line, generate commands to set the line width, move to the start coordinate, draw a line to the end coordinate, and stroke the path. For each circle, generate commands to set the color using the red, green, and blue values, create an arc at the center with the given radius, and fill the shape. For each text element, generate commands to select a standard font at the specified size, move to the coordinates, and show the text string enclosed in parentheses. For example, given title `"Logo"`, a line `(0, 0, 100, 100, 2)`, and a circle `(50, 50, 10, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)`, the output should include "%%Title: Logo", "2 setlinewidth 0 0 moveto 100 100 lineto stroke", and "1.0 0.0 0.0 setrgbcolor 50 50 10 0 360 arc fill".

title: C Header File Generator
spec: Create a tool to generate a C programming language header file from a module description. The entry function is `generate(module, constants, structures, functions)`. The module is a text string representing the module name. The constants contain names and integer values. The structures contain structure names and lists of fields, where each field has a type and a name. The functions contain return types, function names, and lists of parameter types and names. Start the output by generating include guard directives using a capitalized version of the module name. For each constant, generate a macro definition line formatting the name and value. For each structure, generate a structure definition block, iterating through its fields to generate indented lines for each type and name, ending with a semicolon. For each function, generate a prototype line formatting the return type, the function name, and the comma separated parameters inside parentheses, ending with a semicolon. Finish the output by generating the closing include guard directive. For example, given module `"MATH"`, a constant `("PI", 3)`, and a function `("int", "add", [("int", "a"), ("int", "b")])`, the output should include "#ifndef MATH_H", "#define PI 3", and "int add(int a, int b);".

title: VRML 3D Model Exporter
spec: Develop a function to export 3D geometry into virtual reality modeling language text. The entry function is `export(name, vertices, faces, color)`. The name is a text string, the vertices are a list of coordinate triplets, the faces are a list of vertex index triplets, and the color is a triplet of decimal values representing red, green, and blue. Output a standard file header line. Generate a transform node block assigning the provided name. Inside the transform, generate a shape node block. Within the shape, generate an appearance node containing a material node that formats the diffuse color using the provided color values. Next, generate an indexed face set node. Inside this node, generate a coordinate node containing a point field, and format each vertex triplet on its own line. Then, generate a coordinate index field, formatting each face index triplet followed by a negative one to terminate the polygon. For example, given name `"Box"`, a vertex `(1.0, 1.0, -1.0)`, and color `(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)`, the output should include "DEF Box Transform {", "diffuseColor 1.0 0.0 0.0", and "1.0 1.0 -1.0,".

title: Conky Configuration Generator
spec: Write a utility to generate a desktop system monitor configuration script. The entry function is `generate(alignment, width, font, color, widgets)`. The alignment specifies screen placement, the width is an integer, the font is a text string with a size, the color is a hex code, and widgets are a list of monitor items containing a label and a system metric command. Start the output with a configuration block setting the alignment, maximum width, default font, and default color using the provided values. Add lines setting background execution and double buffering to true. Then, generate the text section divider. For each widget, generate a line that formats the widget label in a bold color, followed by the specific system metric command enclosed in the appropriate syntax for the monitor tool. For example, given alignment `"top_right"`, color `"ffffff"`, and a widget `("CPU", "cpu cpu0")`, the output should include "alignment = 'top_right',", "default_color = 'ffffff',", and "${color ffffff}CPU: $color${cpu cpu0}%".

title: Gnuplot Script Builder
spec: Create a program to generate a script for a command line graphing utility. The entry function is `build(filename, title, xaxis, yaxis, datasets)`. The filename is the output image name, the title is the chart title, the xaxis and yaxis contain labels and range limits, and datasets contain a data file path, a line title, and a line color. Output lines to set the terminal type to a high quality image format and specify the output filename. Generate lines to set the chart title, the horizontal axis label, and the vertical axis label. Format lines to set the horizontal range and the vertical range using the provided limits. Finally, generate the plot command. Build the plot command as a single line by iterating through the datasets, formatting each data file path, line title, and line color with the correct plotting directives, separated by commas. For example, given filename `"plot.png"`, title `"Growth"`, and a dataset `("data.txt", "Line 1", "red")`, the output should include "set output 'plot.png'", "set title 'Growth'", and "plot 'data.txt' title 'Line 1' linecolor rgb 'red'".

title: WPA Supplicant Configuration Builder
