spec: Implement a function to generate a wireless network configuration file. The entry function is `generate(interface, networks)`. The interface is the control interface path. The networks are a list where each entry contains a network name, a password, a priority integer, and a boolean indicating if it is a hidden network. Start the output by formatting a line defining the control interface path and a line setting the update configuration flag to one. For each network, generate a network block enclosed in curly braces. Inside the block, format a line setting the network name enclosed in quotes. Format a line setting the pre shared key password enclosed in quotes. Format a line specifying the priority level. If the network is marked as hidden, generate a line setting the scan identifier to one; otherwise set it to zero. Format a line defining the key management protocol as standard personal security. For example, given interface `"/var/run/wpa_supplicant"`, and a network `("HomeNet", "secret123", 5, False)`, the output should include "ctrl_interface=/var/run/wpa_supplicant", "ssid=\"HomeNet\"", and "psk=\"secret123\"".

title: I3 Window Manager Config Builder
spec: Develop a tool to generate a tiling window manager configuration file. The entry function is `configure(modifier, font, terminal, browser, workspaces)`. The modifier is a key like Alt or Super, the font is a text description, the terminal and browser are executable paths, and workspaces are a list of names. Generate a line setting the modifier variable to the provided key. Format a line defining the font setting. Generate a line that binds the modifier plus the enter key to execute the terminal. Format a line that binds the modifier plus a specific key to execute the browser. Generate a line that binds the modifier plus shift and q to kill the focused window. For each workspace in the list, format a line that assigns a numeric key binding combined with the modifier to switch to that workspace name. Also, format a line that assigns a numeric key binding combined with the modifier and shift to move a focused container to that workspace name. For example, given modifier `"Mod4"`, terminal `"urxvt"`, and a workspace `"1: web"`, the output should include "set $mod Mod4", "bindsym $mod+Return exec urxvt", and "bindsym $mod+1 workspace 1: web".

title: Pacman PKGBUILD Generator
spec: Write a utility to generate a package build script for a Linux distribution. The entry function is `generate(name, version, description, architecture, dependencies, source)`. The name, version, and description are text strings. The architecture and dependencies are lists of strings. The source is a web address. Output a text script starting with variable declarations. Format a line for the package name, a line for the package version, and a line setting the package release number to one. Format the description enclosed in quotes. Format the architecture list into a bash array format. Format the dependencies list into a bash array format. Generate a line defining the source array using the provided web address, and a line defining an empty checksum array. Next, generate a build function block containing commands to configure and compile the software using standard make commands. Finally, generate a package function block containing commands to install the compiled files into the package directory variable. For example, given name `"myapp"`, version `"1.0"`, architecture `["x86_64"]`, and a dependency `"glibc"`, the output should include "pkgname=myapp", "pkgver=1.0", "arch=('x86_64')", and "depends=('glibc')".

title: Debian Control File Formatter
spec: Create a program to generate package metadata files for Debian based systems. The entry function is `format(source, maintainer, homepage, binary, architecture, depends, description)`. Generate a multiline text block for the source package. Output a line formatting the source name, a line for the maintainer name and email, a line for the standard build dependencies, a line for the standards version, and a line formatting the homepage web address. Leave a blank line, then generate a block for the binary package. Output a line formatting the binary package name. Format a line specifying the architecture. Format a line combining the provided dependencies with a standard shared library dependency variable. Generate a line for the short description. Finally, take the provided long description, which may contain multiple sentences, and format it so that each sentence begins on a new line indented by a single space, as required by the metadata specification. For example, given source `"hello"`, binary `"hello-bin"`, and description `"A greeting program. It says hello."`, the output should include "Source: hello", "Package: hello-bin", and the description split into " A greeting program.\n It says hello.".

title: HL7 Message Builder
spec: Implement a function to generate a standard health care interoperability text message. The entry function is `build(facility, patient, visit, observation)`. The facility is a clinic name, the patient contains an identifier, a last name, and a first name. The visit contains an account number and an attending doctor name. The observation contains a test code, a result value, and a date. Generate a message header segment formatting the facility name, the current date and time, and the message type code separated by pipe characters. Next, generate a patient identification segment formatting the patient identifier, the last name, and the first name in their respective sequence fields. Generate a patient visit segment formatting the account number and the attending doctor name. Finally, generate an observation segment formatting the test code, the result value, and the observation date. Each segment must begin with its three letter code and be separated by carriage returns, adhering to the strict positional requirements of the protocol. For example, given facility `"CLINIC"`, a patient `("123", "Doe", "John")`, and an observation `("HR", "60", "20231010")`, the output should include "MSH|^~\&|CLINIC|", "PID|||123||Doe^John", and "OBX|||HR||60||||||F|||20231010".

title: Restaurant Receipt Printer
spec: Write a utility to generate a plain text restaurant receipt. The entry function is `print(restaurant, server, table, items, tax)`. The restaurant is a name and address, the server is a name, the table is an integer, the items are a list where each entry has a name, a quantity, and a price, and the tax is a decimal percentage. Start by formatting a centered header block with the restaurant name and address. Generate a line showing the current date and time. Format a line indicating the server name and the table number. Next, generate a divider line made of dashes. For each item, calculate its total price, then format a line showing the quantity, the item name, and the total price aligned to the right. After listing the items, generate another divider line. Calculate the subtotal of all items, the tax amount based on the rate, and the grand total. Format a line for the subtotal, a line for the tax amount, and a line for the grand total. End with a polite closing message. For example, given restaurant `"Joe's Diner"`, server `"Alice"`, tax `0.05`, and an item `("Burger", 2, 5.00)`, the output should include "Server: Alice", "2 Burger 10.00", "Tax 0.50", and "Total 10.50".

title: Bank Statement Text Formatter
spec: Create a text generator for a monthly bank statement. The entry function is `format(bank, account, holder, transactions)`. The bank is a name, the account is a routing and account number, the holder is a name and address, and the transactions are a list where each entry has a date, a description, an amount, and a type (either credit or debit). Start the statement by formatting a header with the bank name and the statement period. Generate a block formatting the account holder name, address, and account details. Define an opening balance of zero. For each transaction, update the balance by adding credits or subtracting debits, then format a line displaying the date, the description padded to a fixed width, the transaction amount, and the running balance. Calculate the sum of all credits and the sum of all debits. Below the transactions, format a summary section showing the total credits, total debits, and the final closing balance, ensuring all currency values are formatted to two decimal places. For example, given bank `"First Bank"`, account `"123456"`, and a transaction `("2023-10-01", "Deposit", 100.00, "credit")`, the output should include "Bank: First Bank", "Account: 123456", and "2023-10-01 Deposit 100.00 100.00".

title: Gym Workout Plan Formatter
spec: Develop a tool to generate a plain text weekly workout schedule. The entry function is `format(title, trainer, weeks, days)`. The title and trainer are text strings, the weeks is an integer count, and days are a list where each entry has a day name, a muscle group focus, and a list of exercises. Each exercise contains a name, the number of sets, the number of repetitions, and a rest duration in seconds. Output a document header formatting the plan title, the trainer name, and the total duration in weeks. Add a blank line, then iterate through the days. For each day, generate a header line formatting the day name and the muscle group focus enclosed in brackets. For each exercise in that day, format a line containing the exercise name followed by the sets, repetitions, and rest time clearly labeled. After listing the exercises for a day, calculate the total number of sets and total rest time, and generate a day summary line formatting these totals. Repeat this block for each day, producing a complete printable schedule. For example, given title `"Strength"`, trainer `"Bob"`, and an exercise `("Squat", 3, 10, 60)`, the output should include "Plan: Strength - By Bob", and "Squat: 3 sets of 10 reps (60s rest)".

title: Weather Forecast Report Builder
spec: Write a function `weather(records)` that takes a list of tuples containing the day name, high temperature, low temperature, and weather condition. It should return a list of formatted strings. Start with a header stating the total number of days in the forecast. Then, for each day, format a string based on the condition. If it is sunny, produce a string about clear skies and the high temperature. If it is rainy, produce a string about precipitation and the low temperature. If snowy, write about freezing temperatures and the high. If cloudy, write about overcast conditions and both temperatures. Also, add an extreme heat warning string if the high temperature is above ninety, or a freeze warning string if the low temperature is below thirty. End with a footer string showing the difference between the maximum high and minimum low across all days. Example input: [("Monday", 95, 70, "sunny"), ("Tuesday", 35, 20, "snowy")]. Example output: ["Forecast for 2 days:", "Monday will have clear skies with a high of 95.", "Extreme heat warning: 95 is very hot!", "Tuesday will see freezing conditions with a high of 35.", "Freeze warning: 20 is very cold!", "Temperature span is 75 degrees."].

title: Museum Exhibit Label Generator
spec: Write a function `exhibit(artifacts)` that takes a list of tuples containing the artifact name, origin year, material, finder name, and current condition. Return a list of display label texts for the museum. Begin with a welcome string mentioning the number of artifacts on display. For each artifact, if the condition is pristine, create a string highlighting its flawless state and the material. If the condition is fragile, create a string warning visitors not to touch the material. If it is restored, create a string mentioning the finder name and the restoration effort. If the finder name is unknown, add a string noting the mysterious origin of the artifact name. Also include a string stating the artifact name and its age calculated from the current year (assume current year is two thousand twenty four). For artifacts older than one thousand years, add an ancient artifact banner string mentioning the origin year. Finally, append a footer string acknowledging the most frequent finder name. Example input: [("Vase", 1900, "Clay", "Smith", "fragile")]. Example output: ["Welcome to our collection of 1 artifacts.", "Please do not touch the fragile Clay.", "Artifact: Vase, age: 124 years old.", "Thank you to our top contributor, Smith."].

title: Police Incident Report Formatter
spec: Write a function `incident(cases)` that takes a list of tuples representing police cases, with elements for case number, crime type, officer name, suspect status, and street name. Return a list of sentences for the daily briefing. The first string must state the total number of cases. For each case, if the crime type is theft, generate a string about property stolen on the street name. If assault, a string about a physical altercation on the street name. If vandalism, a string about property damage handled by the officer name. If the suspect status is arrested, generate a string praising the officer name for the arrest. If at large, generate a string asking for public assistance to find the suspect for the case number. Add a string for each case combining the case number and crime type for the index. End with a string summarizing the number of arrests made. Example input: [("101", "theft", "Jones", "arrested", "Main")]. Example output: ["Daily briefing: 1 cases total.", "Property was stolen on Main.", "Great job Jones on making the arrest.", "Case 101: theft.", "Total arrests today: 1."].

title: Tax Return Summary Generator
spec: Write a function `taxes(filers)` that takes a list of tuples containing filer name, income, deductions, tax bracket percentage, and filing status. Return a list of report lines. Start with a string stating the number of tax returns processed. For each filer, calculate the taxable income and the tax owed. Generate a base summary string with the filer name and tax owed. If the filing status is single, add a string about individual standard deductions applied for the filer name. If married, add a string about joint filing benefits for the filer name. If head of household, add a string about dependent considerations for the filer name. If the tax owed is zero or less, produce a string about a full refund for the filer name. If the tax owed is above ten thousand, produce a string about a high balance due for the filer name. Finally, calculate the total tax collected and return a string stating the total revenue. Example input: [("Alice", 50000, 10000, 20, "single")]. Example output: ["Processing 1 tax returns.", "Alice owes 8000.0 in taxes.", "Individual standard deductions applied for Alice.", "Total revenue collected: 8000.0."].

title: Board Game Turn Summary Formatter
spec: Write a function `turns(actions)` that takes a list of tuples containing player name, action type, resource gained, amount, and target player. Return a list of narrative strings describing the game round. Begin with a string announcing the start of a round with the number of actions. For each action, if the action type is harvest, output a string stating the player name collected the amount of the resource gained. If the action type is steal, output a string stating the player name stole the amount of the resource gained from the target player. If the action type is trade, output a string stating the player name traded the resource gained with the target player. If the action type is build, output a string stating the player name constructed a building using the amount of the resource gained. If the resource gained is magic, output a string noting arcane energy gathered by the player name. If the amount is greater than five, add a string exclaiming a massive play by the player name. Calculate the unique number of players and end with a string stating that number of players competed. Example input: [("Bob", "harvest", "wood", 3, "none"), ("Sue", "steal", "gold", 6, "Bob")]. Example output: ["Round start: 2 actions.", "Bob collected 3 of wood.", "Sue stole 6 of gold from Bob.", "A massive play by Sue!", "A total of 2 players competed."].

title: Vehicle Inspection Report Formatter
spec: Write a function `inspection(vehicles)` that takes a list of tuples containing license plate, make, year, brake condition, and tire tread depth. Return a list of assessment strings. First, output a string with the count of vehicles inspected. For each vehicle, provide a string showing the make and license plate. If the brake condition is poor, add a string warning that the brakes on the make require immediate replacement. If the brake condition is good, add a string noting the brakes on the license plate are in safe working order. If the tire tread depth is below three, produce a string stating the tires on the license plate are bald and dangerous. If the tire tread depth is above eight, produce a string stating the tires on the make are practically new. If the year is older than two thousand, add a string classifying the make as a classic model. End with a string stating the inspection batch is complete for the number of vehicles. Example input: [("ABC1234", "Ford", 1998, "poor", 2)]. Example output: ["Inspected 1 vehicles.", "Vehicle: Ford, plate ABC1234.", "Warning: brakes on the Ford need replacement.", "Tires on ABC1234 are bald and dangerous.", "This Ford is a classic model.", "Inspection batch complete for 1 vehicles."].

title: Garden Planting Calendar Generator
spec: Write a function `garden(plants)` that takes a list of tuples containing plant name, seed type, days to maturity, sunlight requirement, and water frequency. Return a list of gardening instruction strings. Start with a string stating the number of plants in the garden plan. For each plant, output a string with the plant name and days to maturity. If the sunlight requirement is full sun, add a string advising to plant the seed type in the brightest spot. If partial shade, add a string suggesting a spot under a tree for the seed type. If the water frequency is daily, add a string emphasizing that the plant name needs watering every single day. If weekly, add a string noting the plant name requires infrequent watering. If the days to maturity is less than thirty, output a string noting the plant name is a fast growing crop. End with a string wishing the gardener a bountiful harvest of the total number of plants. Example input: [("Tomato", "heirloom", 80, "full sun", "daily")]. Example output: ["Garden plan for 1 plants.", "Tomato takes 80 days to mature.", "Plant the heirloom seeds in the brightest spot.", "Tomato needs watering every single day.", "Wishing you a bountiful harvest of 1 plants!"].

title: Coffee Shop Daily Menu Generator
spec: Write a function `menu(drinks)` that takes a list of tuples containing drink name, size, base coffee, milk type, and price. Return a list of strings representing the menu board. Begin with a string welcoming customers and stating the number of drinks available. For each drink, output a string with the size, drink name, and price. If the milk type is oat, add a string highlighting a dairy free option for the drink name. If the milk type is whole, add a string noting a rich and creamy texture for the drink name. If the base coffee is espresso, add a string warning about a strong caffeine kick from the base coffee. If the base coffee is decaf, add a string offering a jitter free experience for the drink name. If the price is over five, add a string marking the drink name as a premium selection. Finish with a string stating the shop is closing after serving the number of drinks. Example input: [("Latte", "large", "espresso", "oat", 6)]. Example output: ["Welcome! We have 1 drinks today.", "large Latte - 6 dollars.", "Dairy free option available for the Latte.", "Strong caffeine kick from the espresso.", "Latte is a premium selection.", "Shop is closing after serving 1 drinks."].

title: Escape Room Clue Card Generator
spec: Write a function `clues(puzzles)` that takes a list of tuples containing room name, object, hidden item, lock type, and difficulty level. Return a list of strings for the game master to use. Start with a string identifying the total number of puzzles. For each puzzle, output a string directing the players to look in the room name. If the lock type is combination, add a string hinting that numbers are needed to open the object. If the lock type is key, add a string suggesting they search for a physical key for the object. If the difficulty level is easy, output a string stating the hidden item should be a quick find. If the difficulty level is hard, output a string advising them to work together to reveal the hidden item. If the hidden item is a map, add a string stating that navigation in the room name will become easier. Finish with a string reminding players they have sixty minutes to escape the total number of puzzles. Example input: [("Library", "desk", "map", "combination", "hard")]. Example output: ["There are 1 puzzles to solve.", "Direct your attention to the Library.", "You will need numbers to open the desk.", "Work together to reveal the map.", "Navigation in the Library will become easier.", "Remember, you have 60 minutes to escape the 1 puzzles."].

title: Library Overdue Notice Generator
spec: Write a function `notices(borrowers)` that takes a list of tuples containing patron name, book title, days overdue, fine per day, and member type. Return a list of text alerts to send out. Begin with a string stating the total number of notices to send. For each borrower, output a string addressing the patron name and naming the book title.
